articles.title: Robert Griffin III Wants Baylor HC Job After Aranda Fired, QB Won 2011 Heisman Trophy with Bears
articles.summary: Baylor fired head football coach Dave Aranda over the weekend after the team lost its second straight game and fell to 4-3 on the season.
articles.body:
Baylor fired head football coach Dave Aranda over the weekend after the team lost its second straight game and fell to 4-3 on the season.

The Bears came into the 2026 campaign on the heels of four losing seasons in the past six years under Aranda's watch. And former quarterback Robert Griffin III said Monday during an appearance on The Dan Patrick Show that he's interested in becoming the head coach and believes Baylor needs a major change:

Griffin, 36, spent four years at Baylor and was the 2011 Heisman Trophy winner. For his career, he threw for 10,366 yards, 78 touchdowns and 17 interceptions while rushing for 2,254 yards and another 33 scores. In his final season with the team, Baylor went 10-3 and won the Alamo Bowl.

He's undoubtedly a school legend. What he doesn't have, however, is any coaching experience, instead choosing a media career after his time in the NFL was cut short due to injuries. That would make him an extremely risky hire.

To Griffin's credit, he also listed some other candidates he believed would be worthy of the job such as Boise State head coach Spencer Danielson, UTSA head coach Jeff Traylor and a "darkhorse" in USC head coach Lincoln Riley.

And Baylor is an appealing opening, so plenty of experienced options will likely be available to the Bears.

"I think Baylor is a great job," Griffin noted. "It's a university I hold very dear and near to my heart. And the way that coaching happens, being a CEO-type of coach in college football is completely different. And you don't have to have experience coaching at the highest level to be successful. And I'm just tired of seeing Baylor be the stepchild to all of these other teams. We should be back on top."

It's just highly debatable whether Griffin is actually the person capable of getting them there.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or blunder causes confusion - Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe articles published
articles.summary: Harry Kane's dream of winning the Ballon d'Or seemed as if it had come true on Monday when the organisers released an article claiming he had won the award.
articles.body:
For a moment, it seemed as though Harry Kane's dreams of winning the Ballon d'Or had come true.

It was shortly after 17:15 GMT on Monday when an article from the award's official website titled "Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d'Or" began to circulate online.

It was more than four and a half hours before the winner of the game's most prestigious individual award was due to be announced at a star-studded event at London's Palladium Theatre.

The widespread sharing of the article caused confusion online, with some wondering whether France Football - the organisers of the award - had fallen short at the final hurdle of keeping the winner, who was voted for by journalists at the end of September, under wraps.

That was until further digging on the Ballon d'Or website revealed that some of the other favourites to win the award - including Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe - had also had similar pieces penned and published about them.

When asked about the articles by BBC Sport, a Ballon d'Or spokesperson said: "Some profiles of nominees prepared by BallonDor.com were inadvertently published online.

"These articles had been prepared for all nominees and should in no way be considered as an indication of the final results or rankings"

Just before 17:40 BST, the articles about Kane and Mbappe had been removed from the website.

Similar articles were also written about London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas and Barcelona's Ewa Pajor, who are two of the favourites for the corresponding women's award, also taking place on Monday night.

If Kane is to realise his dream and become the first Englishman to win the award since 2001, he will have to wait a little longer to find out.

articles.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Kane, Mbappé and Yamal all declared winners in bizarre official website leak
articles.summary: In a surprising twist, the Ballon d’Or 2026 winners appeared to be leaked online, with Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé, and Lamine Yamal all declared champions before the official ceremony. Fans are left puzzled as the official site published multiple winners leading to speculation and excitement.
articles.body: With the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony underway in London, football fans thought they had discovered the winner before the trophy was even presented, after the award’s official website appeared to publish an article declaring Harry Kane the champion. The excitement quickly turned into confusion when similar articles emerged for Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal, leaving supporters wondering whether the result had been leaked or the organisers had simply prepared their announcements in advance.Harry Kane appears to have won the Ballon d’OrThe Bayern Munich striker initially appeared to have received the biggest individual prize in football after an article titled “Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season” surfaced on the official website. Screenshots spread rapidly across social media, where English supporters began celebrating the apparent confirmation of Kane’s victory.Kane entered the ceremony among the leading contenders after an extraordinary season, with reports highlighting his 73 goals for club and country, although the leaked article referenced a 61-goal season.Mbappe and Yamal articles deepen the confusionThe apparent leak soon became less convincing when articles declaring Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal winners also appeared on the Ballon d’Or website.One headline read, “Kylian Mbappé wins 2026 Ballon d’Or for consistency personified at the very highest level,” while another declared, “Lamine Yamal wins the 2026 Ballon d’Or and sets an unprecedented record!” The pages were reportedly prepared in advance for the possibility of any of the three leading candidates being announced on stage, rather than confirming the actual result.The website subsequently removed the page, while the appearance of all three articles left fans without any reliable indication of who would receive the award.Yamal, Kane and Mbappe had emerged as the leading candidates after outstanding campaigns, with Yamal winning the World Cup with Spain and La Liga with Barcelona, Kane spearheading Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga title and England’s run to the North American World Cup semi-finals, and Mbappe becoming the World Cup’s all-time leading goalscorer while claiming the 2026 Golden Boot.Ballon d’Or countdown continues in LondonThe ceremony is taking place at the London Palladium Theatre, with the main event scheduled to begin at 8pm GMT on Monday, October 26, corresponding to 1.30am IST on Tuesday, October 27.France Football has already begun revealing the lower positions, counting down from 30th to 11th in both the men’s and women’s rankings before the final ten are unveiled individually on stage. The countdown will continue until the leading candidates remain and the official winners are announced, meaning the website’s prematurely published articles have offered no confirmed answer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Robert Griffin III says he is '100%' interested in Baylor's open head coaching job
articles.summary: RGIII won the Heisman Trophy at Baylor in 2011.
articles.body:
Baylor University fired head football coach Dave Aranda over the weekend.

The Bears will conduct a coaching search to find his replacement and may consider a familiar face.

Former quarterback and current NFL and college football analyst Robert Griffin III told Dan Patrick on Monday's edition of the "Dan Patrick Show" that he is "100%" interested in the gig.

"If Baylor wants to get back to winning and have a university that isn't just respectable on the football field, but one the fans can be proud of, they need people who know what it looks like to win at Baylor. "So yeah, I would 100% be interested. I talked with the athletic director, who is a guy in Doug McNamee that knows what it looks like to win at Baylor, know how you have to win at Baylor and recruit to Baylor to make those things happen."

"If Baylor wants to get back to winning and have a university that isn't just respectable on the football field, but one the fans can be proud of, they need people who know what it looks like to win at Baylor.

"So yeah, I would 100% be interested. I talked with the athletic director, who is a guy in Doug McNamee that knows what it looks like to win at Baylor, know how you have to win at Baylor and recruit to Baylor to make those things happen."

Griffin played at Baylor from 2008-11, under then-head coach Art Briles. The Bears went 25-21 in that span, but Griffin's final season was the team's best: Baylor finished 10-3, including a win in the 2011 Alamo Bowl. In 2011, Griffin won the Heisman Trophy, Baylor's only Heisman winner in school history.

It will be interesting to see where the Bears go. Griffin has never been a head football coach and has never coached at any level.

The former quarterback's playing career ended in 2020. The next football season, Griffin signed a deal with ESPN and later joined Fox to cover the NFL and college football.

Baylor hired Aranda ahead of the 2020 season. It was his first time as head coach, and he came from LSU after four years as assistant head coach and defensive coordinator, including on the Tigers' national championship-winning squad in 2019.

The Bears went 2-7 in the COVID-19-shortened season in Aranda's first year, but bounced back in a big way, going 12-2 in 2021, including a Sugar Bowl win. That remains the most wins in a season in school history.

Aranda couldn't sustain that success, as the Bears went 6-7 and 3-9 over the next two seasons. Baylor has been to just three bowl games in the past six years and lost two. Aranda leaves Baylor with a 40-40 record.

The Bears started this season 4-1 but lost to TCU two weeks ago. Then Baylor lost to Kansas this weekend, as the Jayhawks scored the game-winning touchdown with just 1:13 left.

This loss dropped the Bears to 4-3 overall and 2-2 in the Big 12. Baylor announced that defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman will serve as the interim head coach for the remainder of the season. Klanderman has no prior head-coaching experience, but a strong finish to the season could put his name firmly in the mix for the full-time job.

Baylor will go on the road to face UCF this Friday.

Manager Martin O'Neill is sure Colby Donovan is destined for "very big future" as the Celtic full-back extended his contract until 2031.

The 20-year-old has made 15 starts for the Scottish champions this season, having made his debut in August last year.

He was called up to the Scotland squad for the first time in September although he did not feature in any of the four Nations League matches under new boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

"He has come in when we needed him, given everything for our cause," O'Neill told club media, going on to praise the defender's "tremendous attitude".

O'Neill added: "I know the love Colby has for the club and I know what signing this deal means to him and his family.

"I am sure that he will continue to progress and enjoy a very big future in the game, and I am so pleased that he sees his long-term future at Celtic."

Donovan made 27 appearances last season and has been O'Neill's preferred deputy for the injured Alistair Johnston.

"I've loved every single minute," said Donovan, "But it doesn't stop now. I'm just going to keep kicking on.

"You've got to have that belief as a young player coming through here at Celtic. You see all the signings that they bring in.

"When I was a kid, I knew I could come through and do it."

articles.title: Manchester United: Players to return to training on Tuesday but uncertain if Michael Carrick will be in charge
articles.summary: Man Utd beaten 3-0 by Bournemouth at Old Trafford to heap the pressure on head coach Michael Carrick; captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped and United are eight games without a win; players set to return to training on Tuesday after Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox met for talks on Monday
articles.body:
United head coach Carrick was at Carrington on Monday to watch the club's U21s take on Hull in a behind-closed-doors game.

The first-team players had a scheduled day off but Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Jason Wilcox, director of football, also met at the training base, with their talks focused on next steps following Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth .

It remains to be seen what the United hierarchy, which includes Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the part-owner, will decide.

United's defeat to Bournemouth saw Carrick drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench after he questioned his tactics following the 4-1 Champions League loss to Como . It extended United's winless run to eight games across all competitions.

Carrick has overseen United's worst start to a Premier League season. They are 16th in the table , with seven points from their seven games, and just one point adrift of the relegation zone.

Carrick was initially appointed as United boss in January 2026 on a contract until the end of the season, following Ruben Amorim's sacking earlier in that campaign. He delivered a brilliant run of results, winning 12 of 17 matches to earn a third-place finish in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League.

Carrick was nominated for Premier League Manager of the Season and, in May, signed a new contract running to 2028.

How a 'strange day' at Carrington unfolded

"It's been quite a bizarre, strange day at Carrington. This morning, we saw director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada arrive quite early. A few players were in receiving treatment on injuries. Captain Bruno Fernandes, Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko were all in.

"Michael Carrick arrived just before 2pm. From what we understand, he was here to watch the U21s take on Hull City.

"It paints quite an awkward picture. On one end of the car park at Carrington you have the academy building, where Carrick would have been watching the U21s' game, while on the other side you would have had Wilcox and Berrada discussing his future as well as what is the future of Man Utd, what are the next steps potentially in the head coach position.

"As far as we know, no talks between Carrick and Wilcox happened. It's quite tough when you look at the timeline because the game will have finished around 4pm.

"We saw Wilcox leave Carrington around 4.30pm. We understand Carrick left around 4.45pm. Would they have had talks today? It remains to be seen.

"Carrick's future remains in huge doubt and there's no further clarity on whether he will continue or not."

Why there hasn't been swift action on Carrick's future

"I thought this would happen pretty quickly. The fact it hasn't happened makes me think one of two things are going on.

"Probably the most likely is Man Utd's bosses are taking their time to consider who they want as a replacement. The worst-case scenario for Man Utd would be if they sacked Michael Carrick and the person they went for didn't want the job, or they couldn't agree a deal with them and they were left in limbo for days, possibly weeks.

"We know it happens in football all the time - clubs try to set up a replacement before they get rid of the incumbent.

"The second thing is they are very conscious - and it was made clear to them at Old Trafford - just how popular Michael Carrick is among the Man Utd support.

"The same thing happened with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2021 - he gave the most incredible departure video, despite being sacked by Man Utd.

"The club wanted to make sure it ended amicably. I think Man Utd bosses are thinking the same thing here. There might not be an exit video from Carrick but they want this done humanely and respectfully.

"If they don't, the backlash from supporters could be even stronger."

articles.title: Mike McCarthy Reveals Plan for Steelers Safety DeShon Elliott
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers safety DeShon Elliott played 17 snaps in his season debut on Sunday against the New Orleans […]
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers safety DeShon Elliott played 17 snaps in his season debut on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. Elliott has been shelved since last October with a significant hamstring/knee injury that required surgery.

"It was great. I look at his journey, and I can't tell you how much respect I have for him and the way he's attacked this opportunity," Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said during his Monday press conference. "We had him on a play count because we wanted to ease him back into the flow of things, and he needed that chance to get back out there, too. I just expect him to continue to grow. But he definitely cleared that first hurdle. We just needed to get him back on the field."

Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham was also thrilled to see Elliott back.

"Happy to see him out there, great energy on the sideline," Graham said. "My first time to be around him (when he's playing), I know he played a little bit in the preseason. But it was fun to see him out there. The communication stood out. The disguise element. The physicality. It was fun to see him play."

Getting Elliot back is huge for the Steelers, as Rayshawn Jenkins was a major liability during his time with the Steelers. The Steelers cut the veteran last week. Jenkins is now with the Baltimore Ravens .

In the six games Jenkins played for Pittsburgh, he recorded 16 tackles. According to Pro Football Focus, he was targeted five times, allowing five completions for 120 yards, one touchdown, and a perfect 158.3 passer rating.

Elliott opened up on his devastating injury in an interview on Cam Heyward 's Not Just Football podcast this offseason. Elliot told Heyward that he thought it was a Nick Chubb type of situation as soon as he went down with the injury. Chubb's knee injury required two separate, extensive surgeries to repair his MCL, meniscus, ACL, and medial capsule.

"I thought my career was over," Elliott said on Heyward's Not Just Football podcast in April.

The veteran safety said it was just a freak accident.

"Basically a freak accident, a guy landed on my knee, hyperextending my knee," Elliott said. "But the structure of my knee was 100%. I didn't hurt anything in my knee. I actually tore my hamstring. The hamstring, behind my knee, tore off the bone. So, they had to reattach that.

"I've never had non-weight-bearing injuries. Those first two months were pretty hard, and then I finally hit a peak. And after that, it just has been a lot easier now. Now, it is just about getting my strength back and getting my pop back, which is coming along pretty smoothly. Honestly, I've been running really well, jumping, cutting, doing all the things I need to be doing."

Elliott said it was a grueling recovery process.

"They had to reattach that back to my [fibula]. They had to drill a hole through my [fibula] and put a pin through it and reattach that. I was in a brace for six weeks," Elliott said. "I had no weight-bearing for five. Those first two months were so hard. I've been hurt a couple of times in my career, and that was the worst pain when it came to getting my flexion back."

Elliott, who turned 29 in April, is in his eighth NFL season and third with the Steelers. He signed a two-year, $12.5 million contract extension last offseason that will keep him in Pittsburgh through 2027.

Alan Saunders provided reporting from Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Messi makes Ballon d’Or 2026 men’s top 10 finalists on his record 17th nomination, but why has he skipped the ceremony?
articles.summary: Discover why Lionel Messi chose not to attend the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, despite his historic 17th nomination. Learn about his busy schedule with Inter Miami and recent commitments.
articles.body: The biggest names in football have arrived at London’s Palladium for the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, but one familiar face is conspicuously absent from the occasion. Kylian Mbappé, Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal have taken their seats after the red-carpet arrivals, while Lionel Messi, a nominee for the award for the 17th time in his career, is nowhere to be seen. His absence has raised an obvious question, particularly after reports suggested he could play a special role in the ceremony.Messi misses the ceremony as the final countdown beginsThe 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony was due to begin earlier on Monday, October 26, but heavy London traffic pushed the main event at the Palladium back by 30 minutes. The red-carpet arrivals have since wrapped up, with Mbappé drawing attention in a custom suede tuxedo, while Kane and teenage sensation Yamal have also arrived ahead of the announcement.Other prominent attendees include Alexia Putellas, Ousmane Dembélé and former football great Andriy Shevchenko, but Messi will not be joining them in London. The Argentine remains among the 30 nominees and has secured a place in the top 10 of this year’s rankings, making his absence particularly noticeable as the ceremony gets underway.Messi has won the Ballon d’Or a record eight times, most recently in 2023, and has been named among the top 10 finalists for the 2026 award following another impressive campaign with Inter Miami and Argentina. However, his decision to remain in the United States appears to reflect his demanding schedule rather than any lack of interest in football’s most prestigious individual honour.A demanding schedule leaves little room for another flightMessi had only recently returned to the United States after travelling to Oviedo, Spain, to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports. Another transatlantic journey to London would have meant further travel with little time to recover, particularly with Inter Miami approaching an important stage of its MLS campaign.Inter Miami played the New York Red Bulls on October 24 and are scheduled to face FC Cincinnati on October 28, leaving Messi and the coaching staff focused on preparation, rest and recovery. The upcoming fixture carries added importance as the club works towards the MLS play-offs, with Messi still central to its hopes of finishing the season stronglyHe also has responsibilities away from the senior team, with the second edition of the Messi Cup taking place in South Florida from October 25 to November 1. The international under-16 youth tournament is being hosted at Inter Miami’s stadium, and Messi is involved in its organisation, giving him another commitment during the same week as the Ballon d’Or ceremonyThe reported presenter role never materialisedSpeculation about Messi’s possible attendance gathered momentum after reports attributed to independent journalist Juan Jesus suggested that he would attend the ceremony with his family and personally present the trophy to this year’s winner. The idea quickly attracted attention because Messi remains a nominee himself, creating an amusing possibility if he were to win his ninth Ballon d’Or.However, neither Messi’s attendance, his family’s reported presence nor the proposed presenter role had been officially confirmed by France Football or UEFA. Subsequent reporting also indicated that Messi had not received an invitation to present a trophy, with transfer journalist Fabrizio Romano among those reporting that he would not be performing that role.The suggestion that Messi might hand the award to Yamal had also fuelled talk of a symbolic passing of the torch, particularly because the two share a remarkable connection through a 2007 photograph taken for a charity calendar. In the image, a 20-year-old Messi posed with a five-month-old Yamal, long before the youngster emerged as one of football’s leading prospects.That story would have made for a memorable ceremony, but the presenter rumours were never established as fact, and Messi’s absence means the anticipated moment will not take place as reported.A 17th nomination adds another chapter to Messi’s recordMessi’s absence does not diminish the significance of his return to the shortlist after missing out on nominations in the previous two editions. His 2026 campaign included helping Argentina reach the World Cup final, scoring eight goals during the tournament, while he also continued to produce for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer.The nomination takes his total to 17, spanning two decades from his first inclusion in 2006, and leaves him second behind Cristiano Ronaldo, who has received 18 nominations. Messi remains the only player to have won the award while representing a club outside Europe, and his four consecutive victories between 2009 and 2012 remain unmatched.Whether he adds a ninth trophy or watches the outcome from home, Messi’s place among the most decorated players in the award’s history is already secure. articles.title: Why Bengals are in great shape with strength of schedule after 4-2 start
articles.summary: Things have gone well for the Bengals, and it doesn't get any easier going forward.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals just beat the Baltimore Ravens by scoring 35 unanswered points in a dominant 35-13 victory to get to 4-2 on the regular season through seven weeks.

Looking ahead to the remainder of the 2026 season and the Bengals' chances of winning the AFC North, they're actually in fantastic shape despite the 5-2 Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers having a slight advantage heading into Week 8.

Why are they in such great shape? Well, considering the strength of schedule for the remainder of their 2026 campaign, according to Computer Cowboy (@benbbaldwin) on Twitter/x , things are about to get very easy for the Bengals for the rest of the season.

Bengals' strength of schedule makes the rest of 2026 easier than any team has it

"Oh my goodness, the Bengals' remaining schedule," @benbbadlwin commented on the "Remaining Strength of Schedule" update around the NFL prior to Week 7's Monday Night Football matchup.

While plenty of teams have an "easy" schedule this season, none can compare to the Bengals, whose strength of schedule this season is well below 45%, down to roughly 42.5%.

So, how does the Bengals' schedule get so easy? Well, looking at their November matchups paints a clear picture of how easy things will get.

The Bengals face the 1-6 Tennessee Titans in Week 8, followed by the 3-4 Atlanta Falcons in Week 9. They then get the 5-2 Steelers in Week 10 and the 1-4-1 Washington Commanders in Week 11, ending November against the 2-5 New Orleans Saints .

That's a ridiculously easy schedule in November, and while things do get a bit more difficult going forward, it's not an extremely challenging slate either.

They face the 5-2 Cleveland Browns in Week 13, the 5-1 Kansas City Chiefs in Week 14, followed by the 3-3 Carolina Panthers in Week 15, the 2-6 Indianapolis Colts in Week 16, the 4-3 Ravens in Week 17, and finally one more game against the Browns in Week 18.

Over the next 11 games for the Bengals, only the Chiefs are a challenging opponent outside of their AFC North matchups. The Ravens might have Lamar Jackson back, but their team as a whole has some question marks.

Plus, the Steelers and Browns at 5-2 are not especially threatening opponents and are teams this Bengals team can realistically beat.

So, at 4-2, thanks to a very soft schedule for the rest of the season, the Bengals are in great shape to not only make the playoffs, but win the AFC North as well.

articles.title: Everton Takeover Threatens Moyes: Should The Club Change Its Cautious Approach?
articles.summary: Everton’s progress under David Moyes has come under pressure after two consecutive Premier League defeats exposed the limits of their current approach. The T...
articles.body:
Everton's progress under David Moyes has come under pressure after two consecutive Premier League defeats exposed the limits of their current approach. The Toffees lost 2-0 at home to Chelsea before suffering another 2-0 defeat against Arsenal on October 24, leaving the manager with difficult questions to answer about his team's attacking output and ability to compete against stronger opponents.

Despite those setbacks, Everton have collected 10 points from eight league matches, with two wins, four draws and two defeats. They have scored eight goals and conceded nine, while Thierno Barry leads their scoring charts with six goals across all competitions, including three in the league. Everton sit ninth in the table, and face Newcastle United in the EFL Cup fourth round on October 29.

However, the pressure on the pitch coincides with significant uncertainty in the boardroom. The Friedkin Group has reportedly put the club up for sale at a valuation between £800m and £1b, raising fresh questions about the manager's position and Everton's plans beyond the current campaign.

Could Everton's new owners dismiss Moyes immediately?

According to Pete O'Rourke of Football Insider , prospective buyers could remove Moyes as soon as they take control, particularly if they want to appoint their own manager. Transfer correspondent Pete O'Rourke discussed the possibility on the Transfer Insider podcast, while the report highlighted tensions between the Scottish coach and the current ownership.

Moyes has admitted his surprise at the sale announcement and said he has not met or spoken with Dan Friedkin since returning to Everton. His contract expires in 2027, leaving the club facing a decision over whether to offer an extension or allow the final months of his deal to run down.

That uncertainty complicates recruitment and contract planning. Everton need to strengthen a thin squad, develop younger players and manage spending carefully, but a new ownership group may prefer to set its own footballing strategy before approving major commitments. Moyes must therefore balance immediate results with the need to build a side capable of competing for European qualification.

Should Everton's cautious approach change despite Moyes's uncertain future?

HULL, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 11: David Moyes, Manager of Everton, looks on prior to the Premier League 2026/27 match between Hull City and Everton at MKM Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Hull, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images)

Moyes has long favoured defensive organisation, disciplined positioning and hard-working players who protect the team when possession changes hands. That approach can help Everton remain competitive against stronger opponents, yet recent defeats have raised questions about their attacking ambition.

The challenge became particularly clear against Chelsea and Arsenal, when Everton struggled to turn defensive discipline into attacking opportunities. Leaving creative options such as Hayden Hackney and Tyler Dibling out of the starting side against elite opposition may offer greater defensive security, but Everton cannot rely on containment alone if they want to challenge for European places. Barry's scoring contribution gives Moyes a useful focal point, although the team needs better support and more consistent service from midfield.

The ownership situation makes that balance harder to achieve. With no certainty over Moyes's future, Everton must avoid committing substantial transfer fees or long contracts without a clear sporting plan. At the same time, excessive caution could leave the squad short of the quality required to maintain its position.

Moyes could attract interest from Celtic if he leaves Merseyside. Former recruitment figure Mick Brown told the outlet that the 63-year-old would welcome the chance to manage the club where he began his playing career. Celtic's own managerial situation could create an opening, although no appointment has been confirmed.

For Everton, the immediate task remains clear, and that is to secure results, improve the attack and give the next ownership group a competitive squad rather than a collection of unresolved decisions.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal's little brother Keyne makes appearance at Ballon d'Or ceremony
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal was the last of the three favorites for the men's Ballon d'Or to arrive at the ceremony and his little brother, Keyne, was of course part of his...
articles.body:
The real star of the soccer world has arrived!

Keyne, the toddler brother of Spain and FC Barcelona striker Lamine Yamal , walked into the Ballon d'Or award red carpet ceremony holding his father's hand on Monday, Oct. 26 ahead of the delayed ceremony.

Yamal arrived shortly after Keyne and was wearing a black suit with a pointy pink flower on his lapel. He was the last of the three main candidates to arrive at the ceremony with Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé already in the building.

If Yamal, 19, wins the trophy for best soccer player of the year, he would be the youngest player ever to receive the honor.

Keyne captured hearts this summer at the World Cup with his adorable enthusiasm. He cheered on Lamine as the Spanish striker scored his first World Cup goal and won the tournament for La Roja's second men's title.

The toddler has supported Lamine at past Ballon d'Or ceremonies where the FC Barcelona star won the Kopa Trophy award in 2024 and 2025, and was in the crowd when Spain won the 2024 European Championship.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal se acuerda de Cubarsí al ganar el Trofeo Kopa: "Este premio tenía que ser para él"
articles.standfirst: El joven extremo conquista el premio de 'France Football' al mejor jugador menor de 21 años
articles.summary: El joven extremo gana el premio de France Football al mejor jugador menor de 21 años
articles.body: Lamine Yamal sigue haciendo historia. El joven extremo azulgrana fue distinguido hoy con el Trofeo Kopa 2026, galardón anual que entrega la revista francesa France Football para reconocer al mejor futbolista del mundo menor de 21 años. El internacional catalán es premiado con este galardón... ¡por tercer año consecutivo! El Barcelona vuelve a reinar en el Trofeo Kopa y Lamine Yamal sigue asociando su nombre a este reconocimiento. El extremo es acreditado, un año más, con esta distinción cuyo jurado está compuesto exclusivamente por ganadores del Balón de Oro y que se entrega desde 2018 (fue cancelado en 2020 a causa de la pandemia). Es la octava edición del galardón de la revista France Football, y el canterano azulgrana la conquistó por tercera ocasión consecutiva: ya lo recogió en 2024 y en 2025. El primero, lo ganó Mbappé, cuando aún militaba en el PSG; en 2019, De Ligt (Ajax); en 2021, Pedri (Barcelona); en 2022, Gavi (Barcelona); y en 2023, Bellingham (Real Madrid). Lamine suma un nuevo Trofeo Kopa a su palmarés, que no deja de crecer y que es abrumador a pesar de tener sólo 19 años. El extremo internacional conquistó en 2026 LaLiga y la Supercopa de España con el Barcelona y el Mundial con la selección española. El protagonista, fiel a su estilo, quiso compartir el reconocimiento con un compañero. “Me gustaría que estuviera aquí Cubarsí, mi compañero. Este premio tenía que ser para él. Ojalá se lo hubiera llevado él”, señaló Lamine Yamal en referencia al joven central azulgrana, también candidato al galardón. El extremo aprovechó, además, para agradecer el apoyo de sus dos equipos y para marcarse nuevas metas. “Agradecer a mi club y a mi selección. Tengo que seguir trabajando para conseguir títulos colectivos e individuales como este”, apuntó el futbolista de Rocafonda, que insistió en la misma idea al ser preguntado por si era el premio que esperaba recibir esta noche: “Este me hubiera gustado que fuera para Cubarsí”. El atacante de Rocafonda es un fijo en el equipo culé (la temporada 25-26 intervino en 45 encuentros, en los que firmó 24 goles y regaló 18 asistencias, y en esta campaña ya suma 13 compromisos, diez tantos y diez pases finales), y también es titular indiscutible con el combinado nacional de Luis de la Fuente. Con España ha participado, pese a su juventud, en 37 partidos, en los que rubricó 11 dianas. En el Mundial de este pasado verano, fue decisivo: jugó los ocho encuentros, siendo titular en siete. Ahora, Lamine Yamal (que también ganó el Golden Boy en 2024, que entrega el diario deportivo italiano Tuttosport al mejor futbolista del fútbol europeo menor de 21 años) suma su tercer Kopa, que le reconoce como el mejor futbolista del mundo menor de 21 años. Por edad, aún podría ganar un par más...

articles.standfirst: Conoce a todos los premiados de la gala de France Football
articles.summary: Conoce a todos los premiados de la gala de France Football
articles.body: El fútbol mundial viste sus mejores galas para celebrar una cita inolvidable. Este lunes 26 de octubre, el icónico London Palladium se convierte en el epicentro absoluto del deporte rey al acoger la gala del Balón de Oro 2026, una edición repleta de simbolismo por partida doble: no solo rompe con la tradición al trasladar por primera vez su histórica sede de París a la capital británica, sino que además conmemora el 70º aniversario de la creación del galardón por parte de France Football. El futuro del fútbol mundial también tendrá su momento cumbre en la gala con la entrega del Trofeo Kopa, el galardón con el que France Football premia al mejor futbolista menor de 21 años del planeta. Con el recuerdo del histórico triunfo de Lamine Yamal en la edición 2024 y 2025, la nómina de diez finalistas vuelve a poner en valor el irreprimible empuje de las nuevas generaciones. En esta ocasión, jóvenes talentos como el azulgrana Pau Cubarsí, el parisino Warren Zaire-Emery o el madridista Yan Diomandé lideran todas las quinielas para tomar el testigo y consagrarse como la gran promesa reinante del balompié internacional. Finalmente, lo ha vuelto a ganar Lamine Yamal, por tercer año consecutivo. La dirección táctica en el fútbol femenino tendrá su momento de máximo reconocimiento con la entrega del Trofeo Johan Cruyff a la mejor entrenador/a del año femenino. La pugna por la corona de los banquillos se perfila apasionante con una contienda directa entre el técnico azulgrana Pere Romeu, avalado el buen hacer del Barcelona en las competiciones nacionales y continentales, y su antecesor Jonatan Giráldez al frente del deslumbrante proyecto del OL Lyonnes. Frente a la hegemonía de la escuela española, estrategas de primer orden internacional como Andrée Jeglertz (Manchester City), Elena Sadiku (Celtic/BK Häcken) y el seleccionador de Japón Nils Nielsen completan la nómina de finalistas en una categoría que premia la innovación y la regularidad en la élite. El premio se lo llevó Romeu.

articles.title: Vicky López vuelve a ganar el Trofeo Kopa
articles.standfirst: La jugadora del Barcelona repite como el mejor talento emergente del fútbol femenino
articles.summary: La jugadora del Barcelona repite como el mejor talento emergente del fútbol femenino
articles.body: Vicky López volvió a inscribir su nombre en el Trofeo Kopa que reconoce al mejor talento joven en la Gala del Balón de Oro -que este año se celebró en Londres-. Se trata de la segunda edición que se otorga este premio y la segunda vez que recae en la futbolista del Barcelona, que se impuso en la votación final a su compañera Clara Serrajordi, así como a Felicia Schröder, Lily Yohannes y Veerle Buurman. La madrileña volvió a dar un impulso a su proyección, consolidándose como pieza clave tanto del Barcelona campeón de todo (Liga, Copa, Supercopa de España, Champions League) como con la selección española que conquistó la Nations League 2025 y se clasificó para el Mundial de 2027. Vicky jugó con la elástica azulgrana 45 partidos, 31 de ellos como titular, anotando 12 goles y repartiendo 13 asistencias. Por su parte, con la rojigualda disputó 10 encuentros, anotando dos goles y repartiendo una asistencia. En la memoria aún está su gran actuación en el Metropolitano el día que España derrotó a Alemania para reeditar triunfo en la Nations. "Agradezco a France Football y a mis compañeros votantes por ganarlo un año más. No sería posible sin mis compañeras del Barça y la selección, a la familia, a los amigos y especialmente a mi madre, aunque ya no estés a mi lado, mamá te siento en cada paso, gracias mamá por ayudarme a luchar y a no rendirme nunca. Sigamos creciendo y mejorando este deporte juntas. Y gracias Dios por ser un pilar en nuestra vida y bendecirme", explicó Vicky López tras recibir el trofeo a mejor talento joven. La centrocampista sigue así los pasos de Lamine Yamal, único jugador que ha logrado ganar dos Trofeos Kopa de manera consecutiva hasta el momento. Su próximo reto, sin duda, será estar entre las nominadas al Balón de Oro como mejor jugadora del planeta fútbol.
